subject: Renewal: Upshift to 32 GPUs with SLA credit structure proposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: James Ko <james.ko@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — proposal for moving to 32 GPUs

Hi James,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a concise proposal for EdgeWave's renewal window that shifts the dedicated pool from 16→32 GPUs. High-level: a two-year term, a blended per-hour reserved rate, and an SLA credit schedule tied to 95/99th percentile tail latency for the primary inference route.

Key points in this draft:
- Base reserved hours: 24/7 coverage on a 32-GPU pool (vs. current 16) with steady-state hourly pricing.
- Burst allowance: additional on-demand capacity at a capped uplift for traffic spikes.
- Throughput SLO credits: if tail latency exceeds targets on a monthly basis we provide pro-rated credits to the invoice; the credit scale is steeper if both latency and error rate degrade.
- One-time onboarding migration fee to cover model validation and cache warmup scripts.

I attached a short amendment that maps the above to contract language and includes the per-hour numbers (line items). Please review and let me know which parts you want to adjust — particularly the SLO targets and the blended discount table.

Attachment: EdgeWave_renewal_amendment_draft_20270517.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-14T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — proposal for moving to 32 GPUs

Marcus — thanks for sending this over. Team has a few immediate questions before we loop legal:

1) Can you show a blended hourly comparison vs. our current 16-GPU commit (we need to justify cost to finance)?
2) The throughput SLO credit is useful — how are you measuring the tail latency (single region vs. multi-region)? We run across two regions currently.
3) Procurement asks whether the onboarding fee can be amortized across year one rather than paid up front.

Cc'd procurement so they have the draft. We like the burst cap idea; need confirmation that burst won't affect our base-nice-to-have latency guarantees.

Thanks,
James

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: James Ko <james.ko@edgewave.ai>, EdgeWave Procurement <procurement@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — proposal for moving to 32 GPUs

James — great questions. Quick answers and an updated pricing snapshot below. I've also highlighted where we can be flexible.

1) Blended hourly comparison (monthly effective rate) — illustrative: 
- Current 16-GPU reserved: $12.50/hr (effective)
- Proposed 32-GPU reserved: $20.00/hr (blended) — this reflects a volume discount and long-term commit.
- Equivalent per-GPU run-rate ~ $0.625/hr (downside compared to 16-GPU economics since more utilization expected).

2) Tail latency measurement: we will instrument at the request boundary per region (us-east-1/us-west-2). The SLOs in the amendment are per-region and we roll credits only against requests served in the affected region. That prevents cross-region masking.

3) Onboarding fee: we can amortize the $18k onboarding charge across the first 12 invoices (monthly) instead of a one-time payment. If you prefer, we can bake it into the hourly rate for year one and reduce the listed onboarding line.

SLO credit table (excerpt):
- If 95th pct latency > 120ms: 5% credit on monthly reserved hours invoice.
- If 99th pct latency > 300ms: 15% credit.
- Additional 5% credit if monthly error rate > 0.5% concurrently.

I've attached the marked-up amendment that includes these clarifications and two rate alternatives: (A) aggressive discount for 24-month commit, (B) modest discount for 12-month with a mid-term option.

Attachment: EdgeWave_renewal_amendment_draft_20270517.pdf (updated markup)

Next steps: if procurement is comfortable we can hand to legal for redlines. If you'd like, Evelyn can coordinate the technical validation window and Laura can propose an internal signoff timeline.

Best,
Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeWave renewal — request for approval on option A special concession

Team — brief internal note. EdgeWave replied with procurement questions; they're leaning to option A (24-month commit). They asked us to split the onboarding fee and to tighten the 99th pct SLO to 280ms in exchange for earlier signature.

Proposal for internal approval: offer a one-time 3% additional discount on the blended hourly rate (option A) in exchange for signature by 2027-05-31 and agree to the amortized onboarding schedule. This concession reduces first-year ARR by ~4.2% but materially increases committed hours and retention.

Rationale: moving them to 32 GPUs lifts utilization and provides predictable pool fill for Q3 capacity planning. We also get earlier committed spend which improves quarterly bookings.

Please reply with APPROVE or REJECT and any edits to the concession language. If no reply by EOD 2027-05-19 I will assume tacit approval and send the concession email to James.

Thanks,
Marcus
